head: How many members show up in the record?
deck: Records involving Anthropic’s network name 452 of 533 serving members.
note: The network includes Anthropic, its funders, funded groups, and their PACs and lobbyists. A lobbyist’s personal gift or outside spending against a member can put a dot on the chart.
bridge: Did Anthropic’s employees and PAC give to members’ committees?

head: Did Anthropic’s employees and PAC give to members’ committees?
deck: Yes, and their gifts reached committees linked to 199 serving members by Sept. 30, 2026, up from 10 at the end of 2024.
note: Employee gifts are personal money. PAC gifts come from Anthropic’s political action committee. Employment is as reported to the FEC, and amounts are before refunds.
bridge: Who did outside groups spend against?
source: FEC contributions to campaigns, leadership PACs and single-member joint fundraising committees

head: Who did outside groups spend against?
deck: 74% of the outside spending shown went against Republicans, using money from all donors.
note: The filings identify the committee that spent the money. They cannot trace an expenditure to a donor or establish coordination with a candidate.

head: How big was the network in federal AI lobbying?
deck: On 2025 filings naming AI, network clients reported 0.5% of the total, while frontier labs reported 6%.
note: Each amount covers all issues on a filing and gives an upper bound on AI lobbying. Outside-firm fees included in a client’s own reports count once.
bridge: Which bills came up most in reports filed for Anthropic?

head: Which bills came up most in reports filed for Anthropic?
deck: Chip proposals led among individual bills named in the reports.
note: The counts cover bill mentions only. A mention leaves the company’s position open.
bridge: Did sponsors of the named bills get campaign gifts?
source: Federal lobbying reports and Congress.gov bill records

head: Did sponsors of the named bills get campaign gifts?
deck: Serving sponsors of stand-alone bills in reports filed for Anthropic had campaign gifts on file more often than serving members overall.
note: The records give no link between a gift and a bill.
bridge: Did House offices and political committees pay Anthropic?
source: Senate quarterly lobbying reports, Congress.gov bill records and FEC contribution filings

head: Did House offices and political committees pay Anthropic?
deck: Yes, and they paid OpenAI 2.3 times as much in the spending records collected here.
note: These payments were purchases, including Claude and ChatGPT. Committee coverage is partial, and card descriptions may bundle charges.

head: Does every tie mean the same thing?
deck: Ted Lieu and Thom Tillis each add one seat to the count, for different kinds of records.
